title: Anthropic’s $2trn IPO is priced below what AI stocks already fetch
excerpt: Six backers told the FT they expect a $2 trillion Anthropic IPO in October. On the revenue Anthropic last disclosed, that is 43 times sales.
content_html:
The number comes from investors, not the company. Six backers told the Financial Times that rising revenue would let the five-year-old lab more than double its valuation in an autumn listing.

At $2 trillion it would eclipse SpaceX, which went public at $1.77 trillion in June.

Anthropic itself has fixed nothing. Several investors said senior executives had not settled on a target, even privately. The models are the investors’ own.

The machinery is moving regardless. Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan are leading the offering, Quartz reported.

Three bulge-bracket banks on a mandate is not a rumour. It is the difference between investors discussing a listing and a listing being built.

The revenue, and the caveat attached to it

Two figures matter. In May the company said its annualised revenue had passed $47bn, which is the last number Anthropic disclosed itself.

Investors now expect that to reach $100bn to $120bn by the end of 2026, a rise of more than ten times across the year.

Read the definition before the number. Annualised revenue is Anthropic’s preferred measure. It infers full-year sales from recent performance rather than counting a year of receipts.

That is a legitimate way for a fast-growing company to describe itself. It also means a strong month flatters the figure. It is not the number a public company reports.

The multiple is less mad than it sounds

Run the arithmetic on the disclosed figure. At $2 trillion against $47bn, Anthropic would trade at roughly 43 times revenue.

Anthropic has no listed American peer to price against. But companies treated as AI beneficiaries have traded this year at about 55 times revenue, the FT notes, naming Palantir and the cloud group Nebius.

On that comparison, $2 trillion is not an outlier. It is below where the market already values businesses with a fraction of Anthropic’s growth rate.

One of the investors went further. “If Anthropic is growing 800 percent a year, you’d think at the incredibly low end they would trade at 30 times,” the person said. “That would make them a $3 trillion company.”

The first risk is the American government

Here is what the multiple does not price. Anthropic is in active litigation against the Department of Defense, which labelled it a supply-chain risk.

In June the Commerce Department hit the company with export controls, and Anthropic briefly pulled Fable 5 and Mythos 5, its two leading models.

That episode has a number attached. Two investors told the FT the temporary ban slowed revenue growth in June, before the company rebounded.

So a regulator bent the growth curve once already this year, inside a single month. The episode also spooked customers who had built on those models.

The second risk is that customers are looking at the bill

Anthropic’s market-leading model costs more than two and a half times as much to use as OpenAI’s flagship, according to Artificial Analysis. Chinese open-weight models cost a fraction of either, and they improved sharply this year.

The company gained market share among US businesses last month, on payments data from Ramp. The same analysts found those businesses were “hitting their limit on AI spend”. Many are moving to cheaper alternatives.

Some have gone further than switching models. Faced with rising costs, certain customers have reversed internal instructions telling employees to maximise their AI use.

That is the uncomfortable pairing. Anthropic is winning share in a market whose buyers want to spend less, while Chinese models keep closing in on capability.

Why the company is saying nothing

Anthropic declined to comment, and it has a reason beyond preference. It filed confidentially with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June. That puts it in a quiet period, limiting what it can say about its finances.

So every number in circulation comes from investors who stand to gain from the listing. That is not a reason to dismiss them. It is a reason to attribute them carefully.

The money behind those models is not small. Venture capitalists, sovereign wealth funds and other institutions have put just under $100bn into the company during 2026 alone.

Its valuation passed OpenAI’s for the first time in May, at $965bn post-money, and secondary trades have since marked it at $1.2 trillion.

What the bulls actually say

The case for is worth stating in its own words. Anthropic has spent the year releasing models that outperformed rivals, and selling them to businesses rather than consumers.

One investor, who has also backed OpenAI and SpaceX, put it plainly to the FT. “It’s easy to come up with challenges,” the person said. The company “continues to be in first position in performance, positioning, and what people want exposure to”.

There is truth in that last clause. A listing this size is partly a bet on investor appetite for AI exposure, and appetite is not the same thing as fundamentals.

Which is why the FT frames the risk as a market one. A float at $2 trillion would test public markets that are growing more nervous about the AI boom.

What would settle it

Two things, and the first is close. A public S-1 replaces every investor model with audited revenue. It will show whether the $47bn disclosed in May grew the way the projections assume.

The second is the June dip. If one month of export controls measurably slowed growth, the filing will show it. That line matters more than the headline number.

Until then the honest summary is narrow. The multiple is defensible on the numbers available. But the company cannot confirm them, its customers are trying to spend less, and its own government has already switched its best products off once.

content_html_zh:
这个数字来自投资者，而不是公司。 六名支持者告诉英国《金融时报》，收入的增加将使这家成立五年的实验室在秋季上市时的估值增加一倍以上。

其 2 万亿美元的市值将超过 SpaceX，后者 6 月份上市时的市值为 1.77 万亿美元。

人择本身并没有解决任何问题。 一些投资者表示，高管们尚未确定目标，即使私下也是如此。 这些模型是投资者自己的。

不管怎样，机器都在移动。 据 Quartz 报道，摩根士丹利、高盛和摩根大通牵头此次发行。

三个大银行受委托并不是谣言。 这是投资者讨论上市和正在建设的上市之间的区别。

收入及其附带的警告

两个数字很重要。 5 月份，该公司表示其年化收入已超过 470 亿美元，这是 Anthropic 自己披露的最后一个数字。

投资者现在预计，到 2026 年底，这一数字将达到 1000 亿至 1200 亿美元，全年增长十倍以上。

请阅读数字之前的定义。 年化收入是 Anthropic 的首选衡量标准。 它根据最近的表现推断全年销售额，而不是计算一年的收入。

对于一家快速发展的公司来说，这是描述自己的合法方式。 这也意味着强劲的月份使这一数字更加美好。 这不是上市公司报告的数字。

倍数并不像听起来那么疯狂

对公开的数字进行算术运算。 Anthropic 的股价为 2 万亿美元，相对于 470 亿美元，其交易价格约为收入的 43 倍。

Anthropic 没有上市的美国同行可以与之竞争。 但英国《金融时报》指出，被视为人工智能受益者的公司今年的股价约为收入的 55 倍，并提到了 Palantir 和云集团 Nebius。

相比之下，2 万亿美元并不是一个异常值。 它低于市场已经对 Anthropic 增长率一小部分企业的估值。

一位投资者走得更远。 这位人士表示：“如果 Anthropic 每年增长 800%，你会认为在低得令人难以置信的情况下，他们的交易价格会是 30 倍。” “这将使他们成为一家价值 3 万亿美元的公司。”

第一个风险是美国政府

这是倍数未定价的内容。 Anthropic 正在积极针对国防部提起诉讼，国防部将其标记为供应链风险。

6 月，美国商务部对该公司实施了出口管制，Anthropic 一度下架了其两款主导游戏《神鬼寓言 5》和《神话 5》。

该集附有编号。 两名投资者告诉英国《金融时报》，临时禁令导致公司 6 月份营收增长放缓，随后该公司出现反弹。

因此，今年监管机构在一个月内就已经弯曲了一次增长曲线。 这一事件也吓坏了使用这些模型的客户。

第二个风险是客户看账单

根据 Artificial Analysis 的数据，Anthropic 市场领先的模型的使用成本是 OpenAI 旗舰模型的两倍半以上。 中国的开放式重量型号的成本只是这两种型号的一小部分，而且今年的价格有了大幅提高。

上个月，凭借 Ramp 的支付数据，该公司在美国企业中的市场份额有所增加。 同一批分析师发现，这些企业“在人工智能方面的支出已达到极限”。 许多人正在转向更便宜的替代品。

有些人所做的不仅仅是转换模型。 面对成本上升，某些客户改变了内部指示，要求员工最大限度地利用人工智能。

这就是不舒服的配对。 Anthropic 正在赢得买家希望减少支出的市场份额，而中国模式则不断逼近其能力。

为什么公司什么也没说

Anthropic拒绝发表评论，其原因超出了偏好。 该公司于六月向美国证券交易委员会秘密提交文件。 这使得它处于一个安静的时期，限制了它对其财务状况的评论。

因此，流通中的每一个数字都来自那些有望从上市中获利的投资者。 这并不是解雇他们的理由。 这是仔细归因它们的一个原因。

这些模型背后的资金并不小。 仅 2026 年，风险投资家、主权财富基金和其他机构就向该公司投资了近 1000 亿美元。

其估值在 5 月份首次超过 OpenAI，达到 9650 亿美元的融资后估值，此后二级交易估值已达到 1.2 万亿美元。

多头实际上说了什么

这个案例值得用它自己的话来说明。 Anthropic 花了一年的时间发布了优于竞争对手的模型，并将其出售给企业而不是消费者。

一位也支持 OpenAI 和 SpaceX 的投资者向英国《金融时报》直白地表达了这一点。 “提出挑战很容易，”该人士表示。 该公司“在业绩、定位和人们想要接触的内容方面继续处于领先地位”。

最后一句话是有道理的。 如此规模的上市在一定程度上是对投资者对人工智能投资兴趣的押注，而兴趣与基本面并不是一回事。

这就是为什么英国《金融时报》将风险定义为市场风险。 2万亿美元的发行量将考验对人工智能热潮越来越紧张的公共市场。

什么可以解决它

有两件事，第一件事很接近。 公开 S-1 用经过审计的收入取代了每个投资者模型。 它将显示 5 月份披露的 470 亿美元是否按照预测的方式增长。

第二个是六月份的下跌。 如果一个月的出口管制明显减缓了经济增长，文件就会显示这一点。 这句话比标题数字更重要。

在那之前，诚实的总结是狭隘的。 从现有的数字来看，这个倍数是站得住脚的。 但该公司无法证实这些消息，其客户正试图减少支出，而且其本国政府已经关闭了一次最好的产品。
